title: The Tools Primitive: Calling Actions and Reading Their Results

questions.question: A tools/list request already returned some tools and a nextCursor of an empty string, not an absent field. What should a client do next?
options: Send another tools/list request with cursor set to the empty string, since presence alone signals more
Stop paging right away, since an empty nextCursor value must always mean the server has nothing left to send
Repeat the exact same request again with no cursor at all, since an empty string can never be a valid cursor
Wait patiently for a notifications/tools/list_changed message before ever requesting another page at all
questions.explanation: A nextCursor being present in the result, even as an empty string, means more tools may be available; only the field's absence signals that the list is finished.

questions.question: A tool call succeeds and the server's result omits isError entirely. How must a conformant client read that result?
options: As isError true, because a missing field always defaults to the more cautious reading
As invalid, because CallToolResult requires isError to be present on every single result
As isError false, since an absent isError field means the whole tool call succeeded
As undefined, so the client must ask the server which value it actually intended
questions.explanation: CallToolResult treats a missing isError as false; the field only needs to appear, set to true, when the tool itself ran into a problem.

questions.question: A client calls tools/call naming a tool the server never registered. Which response fits MCP 2026-07-28?
options: A JSON-RPC error with code -32601, since the method itself could not be located on the server
A JSON-RPC error with code -32602, since the call names a tool the server never registered
A normal result with isError set to true and an empty content list carried back
An input_required result asking the client to choose a different tool right away
questions.explanation: An unknown tool is a protocol error, code -32602 Invalid params; -32601 is reserved for a JSON-RPC method the server has never heard of, not a missing tool.

questions.question: A tool definition ships with no annotations object at all. What must a client assume about its behavior?
options: readOnlyHint true and destructiveHint false, the single safest combination the schema allows
The tool cannot be listed at all until the server supplies annotations explicitly
The tool quietly inherits the annotations of the last tool the client called
readOnlyHint false, destructiveHint true, idempotentHint false, openWorldHint true, the schema defaults
questions.explanation: ToolAnnotations defaults to readOnlyHint false, destructiveHint true, idempotentHint false, and openWorldHint true; an absent annotations object leaves the client with those cautious defaults, not a safe assumption.

questions.question: A server's tool list grows by one entry while a client already has a subscriptions/listen stream open with toolsListChanged set to true. How does the client find out?
options: The server sends notifications/tools/list_changed on that stream, tagged with its subscription id
The client must close and reopen its entire connection before any new tool ever becomes visible
The next tools/call response quietly folds the brand new tool into its own content list
The server resends the entire tools/list result completely unprompted on that same open stream
questions.explanation: A subscribed client learns of a changed tool list through notifications/tools/list_changed, carrying the same subscriptionId as the listen request that opened the stream, and then re-fetches with an ordinary tools/list.

questions.question: A tool needs to point the model at a large file instead of inlining its contents in the result. Which content block fits, and what must it carry at minimum?
options: A resource block, carrying the file's full text or base64 blob inline in the result
A text block, carrying the file's path as a plain string with no other fields
An image block, carrying the file rendered as a small preview thumbnail
A resource_link block, carrying at least the file's uri and a name
questions.explanation: A resource_link block points at a resource by uri and name instead of inlining it, which fits large content the model may never need to read in full.
